evals.prompt: sdd-harden is processing wp-04 and two approaches surfaced: (A) migrate the session store to Redis with a new abstraction layer, (B) extend the existing in-memory store with a TTL eviction policy. The spec marks this section decision-required. Arbitrate.
evals.expected_output: Normalizes both approaches along seven axes (objective, assumptions, files touched, sequencing, validation, rollback, cost), cross-reviews dimension-by-dimension, and emits a decision memo with chosen direction, rejected alternative with reason, and verification gates for the chosen path.
expectations: SKILL.md describes normalizing each approach into seven axes before comparison
SKILL.md describes emitting a decision memo with chosen direction, rejected alternatives, and verification gates
SKILL.md states the memo is advisory input to sdd-harden and does not alter WP frontmatter status

evals.prompt: sdd-arbiter produced a decision memo recommending approach B. Can sdd-arbiter advance the WP from hardened to ready now?
evals.expected_output: No — sdd-arbiter is advisory only. It does not change the human-gated hardened→ready transition. Status authority stays with the human gate in sdd-harden.
expectations: SKILL.md states sdd-arbiter does NOT change the human-gated hardened→ready transition
SKILL.md states status authority remains exclusively with the human gate in sdd-harden
SKILL.md Advisory Boundary section is present and unambiguous

evals.prompt: sdd-harden is hardening wp-07. Only one approach exists in the spec — add an index to the users table. Should sdd-arbiter run?
evals.expected_output: No arbitration needed — a single approach with no competing option does not warrant sdd-arbiter. Return immediately noting arbitration is not applicable.
expectations: SKILL.md states a single approach with no competing option does not warrant arbitration
SKILL.md Gotchas document the single-approach skip rule

evals.prompt: Can you use sdd-arbiter to pick the best color scheme for a dashboard UI?
evals.expected_output: sdd-arbiter should NOT trigger — this is a UI styling decision, not an SDD WP approach arbitration with a hard-to-reverse bet. Not applicable.
expectations: SKILL.md trigger requires decision-required in a WP spec OR two or more hard-to-reverse approaches
A UI color scheme choice is outside the trigger surface of sdd-arbiter (no hard-to-reverse architectural bet)
